The applicant or any property owner entitled to notice of the hearing may, within fifteen days after the date of the Planning Commission decision, appeal the Planning Commission decision to the City Council (Ord. No. 091-529). A fee is required for filing an appeal with the City Clerkâ€™s office (R05-14).
The Council may, within fifteen days after the date of the decision or on or before the first date following the first Council meeting after the date of the Planning Commission decision, whichever occurs last: 1) Confirm the action of the Planning Commission and grant or deny the application; 2) Set the matter for public hearing and dispose of it in the same manner as on an appeal; or 3) Amend, modify, delete or add any condition of approval which the Council finds is not substantial under the circumstances relative to or affecting the property subject to the application for a development entitlement. MINUTES OF THE MARCH 29, 2022
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

A Teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates Planning Commission was held
via Zoom videoconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and
pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s
recommended measures to promote social distancing. Members of the public were
provided with the following information to provide public input:

  BY COMPUTER: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/84236887271
  Zoom Meeting ID: 842 3688 7271 or
  BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code 842 3688 7271 #

CALL TO ORDER: 5:40 p.m.

ROLL CALL

Present: Commissioners Thomas, Nendick, Wade, Lazzaro

Also Present: Acting Community Development Director Brady, City Attorney, Cotti,
Assistant City Attorney Crosthwaite

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

None.

  PUBLIC HEARING

  1. An Ordinance of the City of Palos Verdes Estates, California amending
  Section 18.20.010 (La Venta Inn) of Chapter 18.20 (Specific Exceptions) of
  Title 18 (Zoning Regulations) of the Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code
  and finding the action exempt from the California Environmental Quality
  Act.

Assistant City Attorney Crosthwaite presented the staff report, providing background
on the issue as well as the ordinance originally adopted in 1948. She presented a
brief history on the tenants and the issue with the original ordinance not providing a
clear understanding of the regulations. Ms. Crosthwaite provided background on the
ordinance that went to the Planning Commission in January at which time there was
discussion and direction given to staff to staff.

She reviewed all of the revisions that have been made to the proposed Ordinance
based on the Commission’s previous directions. The Commissioners asked
questions of the Assistant City Attorney.

The Public Hearing was opened.

The following individuals addressed the Commission in favor:
Virginia Butler  Arlo Sorenson
Joan Davidson  Diane Williams
Kathleen Panccuci  Douglas Bigley
 Mark Matthews
Jen Hardwick
Timmi Hallem
Jason Buck
Meg Walker
Duncan Blunt
Tamara Suminski

The following individuals addressed the Commission with concerns:
Joseph DiSanto  Rick Connor
Wilma Shrek  Darcel Ramirez Hamson
Sandra Damiani  Clark Koury
John Williams  Stacey Nozaki
Edward McNamara  Stephanie
Joel Damiani  Sara Aikin
Marianne Cronin
Kristen
Steve Goldsmith
Robert Aikin
Blake Gilman
Lew Gildred
Julie Kassouf
Jim Parker
Andrew Garland

The public hearing was closed
The Commissioners asked numerous questions of Mark Matthews and Meg Walker,
and some of the speakers regarding the decibel level of the sound, the hours of
operation, restricting the use of the outdoor patio and courtyard after a certain time,
and other issues that were raised by members of the public.

The Commissioners deliberated at length and provided the following direction to staff:
(1) add language to the Ordinance that limits the size of buses to shuttle buses and
require loading and unloading of passengers to occur within the parking lot of the
property; (2) in Section 3(a) research what other local communities have in their
requirements for sound, and identify and include decimal number metrics for
amplification; add to Section 3(d) that the doors to the patio and courtyard be closed at
8:30 pm when amplified music is playing; (3) validate the maximum capacity of the
building to determine the maximum number of people; (4) in Section 3(g) delete the last
sentence of that paragraph, and add a limit to the number of special permits that can
be issued per year; (5) add language that enforcement of the rules and regulations be
self-enforced by the event operator; (6) revise Section E of the ordinance to have the
Planning Commission review compliance with the provisions of Section 18.20.010
within the first year of adoption of the Ordinance.

ACTION: Moved by Chairman Lazzaro, and seconded by Vice-Chair Wade, to continue
this matter to the next reasonably available date in approximately two weeks with the
recommended revisions to the ordinance as directed. The motion unanimously carried
by the following roll call vote:
AYES: Thomas, Nendick, Wade, Lazzaro
NOES: None

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business to come before the Commission he meeting was
adjourned at 9:31 pm to a Special Meeting within the next two weeks at 5:30 pm.

Respectfully submitted

___________________________________
Sheryl Brady, Secretary
